To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Imiquimod and the two novel compounds, S-2769 and S-2846, induce cytokines and specific cytokine mRNAs in monkeys.
the imidazoquinoline immune response modifiers, S-27659 and S-28464, induce cytokines and their specific mRNAs in cynomolguses monkeys.
the imidazoquinoline, S-2843, induced the production of cytokines in the blood and skin of cynomolgus macaques, which are used as a model for human disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new family of immune response modifiers.
the development of new antiviral and immunotherapeutic agents.
the development of novel compounds that induce the immune system to produce cytokines and cytokines specific mRNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the induction of cytokine specific mRNA and protein in monkeys is a useful tool in the evaluation of immune response modifiers.
the imidazoquinoline compounds, imiquimol, S-27608, and S-28464, induce the expression of cytokines and cytokines specific mRNAs in cynomolgous monkey PBMC and skin.
imidazoquionolines stimulate cytokine production in monkeys.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the imidazoquinoline S-27609, which is the most effective antiviral agent in vitro of the imidazoquionolines, has the least ability of the three compounds to induce cytokines, and that the imidazolquinoline S-28463 is the most effective of the three compounds in vivo.
the induction of cytokine mRNA and proteins by imiquimod and S-28464 are comparable in monkeys and humans.
the imidazoquinoline compounds, imiquimol, S-27608 and S-28464, are potent inducers of cytokines in human and monkey cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
imiquimod and imidazoquinoline analogs induce cytokine expression in non-human primates.
the cynomolgus monkey is a suitable model for evaluating the cytokine induction potential of imidazoquinoline drugs.
the imidazoquinoline compounds induce cytokines and specific mRNA in cyno PBMCs.
